_meta.description: Verified catalog of Kubernetes kubelet-config / control-plane component-flag config-breakers (Phase 3 of the Upgrade Breakage Radar). Consumed by ConfigBreakerCatalog for ConfigBreakerAnalyzer. Closes the node-level blind spot Phase 1 (removed APIs) and Phase 2 (removed in-tree volume plugins) cannot see: a config FIELD or CLI FLAG whose semantics change or which is outright removed at a specific Kubernetes version, independent of the Pod/apps-v1 API schema (which never changes under the GA compatibility guarantee).
_meta.verificationMethod: Every appliesFromVersion/deprecatedInVersion value below was read directly from the official kubernetes/kubernetes CHANGELOG-<version>.md files (raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/master/CHANGELOG/) and, where the field/flag's very existence needed independent confirmation, the upstream Go source (k8s.io/kubelet/config/v1beta1/types.go, pkg/kubelet/apis/config/v1beta1/defaults.go). Exact source URL + matched sentence is recorded per-entry below in `provenance`. NONE of these values were hand-typed from memory.
_meta.nonDetectableNote: rtz-k8s-kubelet-cadvisor-legacy-flags-removed is VERIFIED (real, cited CHANGELOG entry) but marked detectable=false: it is a kubelet-process CLI-only flag set never exposed via /configz (confirmed absent from the typed KubeletConfiguration struct) and the kubelet itself has no Kubernetes Pod/static-pod representation to scan for command[]/args[] — neither of Phase 3's two collection surfaces can see it. ConfigBreakerAnalyzer filters out non-detectable rules so this NEVER silently reports 'clean'; it is documented here for transparency/backlog only. See the entry's own `note` field for the full reasoning. Step 2 (2026-07-11) added 3 more verified-but-non-detectable kubelet-CLI-only flag rules (--runonce, --cloud-config, --pod-infra-container-image) for the SAME structural reason: kubelet is a host-level process with no static-pod command[]/args[] representation for this catalog's componentFlag collection surface to scan. Step 3 (2026-07-11) added 8 more kubelet-only-CLI-flag non-detectable rules (--experimental-check-node-capabilities-before-mount, --non-masquerade-cidr, --experimental-kernel-memcg-notification, --master-service-namespace [kubelet variant], --keep-terminated-pod-volumes, --iptables-masquerade-bit/--iptables-drop-bit) for the same structural reason, plus 1 non-detectable kube-proxy CLI-flag rule (--resource-container) since kube-proxy (a DaemonSet, not a static pod) is outside this catalog collection surface entirely. Total non-detectable: 12.
_meta.step2Note: Step 2 (2026-07-11) extended this catalog with 52 feature-gate/CLI-flag removal rules covering Kubernetes 1.32-1.37 (39 feature-gate removals via the NEW featureGateList/featureGateMap matching logic, plus 13 standalone CLI-flag/kubeletConfig-field rules: --runonce x2, --cloud-provider/--cloud-config x2, --pod-infra-container-image, failCgroupV1). See _workspace/step2_summary.md for full per-rule provenance and the honesty caveats (component-scoping assumptions, locked-vs-removed distinction).
_meta.coveredThroughVersion: 1.16-1.37 (Step 3, 2026-07-11, extended the 1.32-1.37 Step 2 range back to 1.16)
_meta.step3Note: Step 3 (2026-07-11) backfilled the config-breaker catalog with the older-release (1.16-1.31) config/flag class: 109 feature-gate removal/lock rules (one rule per individual gate name, deduped across releases per the earliest-breaking-version rule -- see _workspace/step3_load_summary.md for the full per-rule dedup log), 22 removed component CLI-flag rules (12 detectable across kube-apiserver/kube-scheduler/kube-controller-manager; 10 marked detectable=false -- kubelet-only flags with no static-pod representation, or kube-proxy which this catalog's collection surface does not scan), and 1 new kubeletConfig nested-selector rule (memorySwap.swapBehavior=UnlimitedSwap dropped at 1.30) that required a minimal backward-compatible dotted-path extension to ConfigBreakerAnalyzer.matchesKubeletConfigRule. Also enriched the existing rtz-k8s-gate-removed-server-side-apply (1.32) rule with a newly-verified deprecatedInVersion=1.26 lock precursor rather than creating a duplicate rule. Total: 55 -> 187 rules.
_meta.step4Note: Step 4 (2026-07-12) closed the 1.34-1.36 feature-gate/flag removal gap found by the 1.32->1.37 coverage audit: added PodDisruptionConditions (1.34 #129501), StrictCostEnforcementForVAP + StrictCostEnforcementForWebhooks (1.35 #134994, locked 1.32), HonorPVReclaimPolicy (1.36 #135335, locked 1.33), WatchFromStorageWithoutResourceVersion (1.36 #136066) as CRITICAL control-plane gate breakers, plus --register-schedulable kubelet flag (1.34 #122384, detectable=false). Excluded the kube-proxy iptables-wait change (#131961) as an internal iptables-binary detail, not a user-facing flag.
_meta.step5Note: Step 5 (2026-07-12) closed removed-feature-gate gaps found by the parallel per-release 1.32->1.37 changelog audit: 8 control-plane gate removals (DRAControlPlaneController 1.32 #128003, DevicePluginCDIDevices + LegacySidecarContainers 1.34 #132083/#131463, SizeMemoryBackedVolumes + UserNamespacesPodSecurityStandards 1.35 #133720/#132157, CSIMigrationPortworx + InTreePluginPortworxUnregister 1.36 #135322, DeclarativeValidationTakeover 1.37 #139212) + 3 -kubelet featureGateMap variants for the node-read gates. All verbatim-sourced.
_meta.step6Note: 2026-08-31 locked-gate class (source-derived by scripts/gen-locked-gate-rules.py from LockToDefault: true diffs across v1.31.0..v1.35.0 of pkg/features/kube_features.go + the apiserver registry): 146 rules / 73 gates across 1.32-1.35 using the new featureGateListValueEquals / featureGateMapValueEquals conditions — a gate locked while explicitly set to the non-default value is the same fatal startup failure as a removed gate, which this catalog previously could not see. Counts are deliberately NOT changelog-derived: the changelogs under-report locks and mis-stated two lock versions (MaxUnavailableStatefulSet, StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC).

rules.title: kube-controller-manager flag --concurrent-service-syncs was removed in Kubernetes 1.37
rules.remediation: Remove --concurrent-service-syncs from the kube-controller-manager static-pod command/args before upgrading to 1.37+. The flag has been a no-op since v1.31 (present-but-ignored) and is fully removed (kube-controller-manager will fail to start with an unrecognized-flag error) at 1.37.
rules.note: Both the deprecatedInVersion (no-op since v1.31) and appliesFromVersion (removed in 1.37) facts come from the SAME single verified CHANGELOG-1.37.md sentence — not independently cross-checked against a CHANGELOG-1.31.md entry (a 'silently becomes a no-op' event does not always get its own release note; only the later actual removal does, which is exactly the 1.37 entry cited below). No fabrication: this is a direct quote of the real upstream release note.

provenance.name: kubernetes/kubernetes CHANGELOG-1.37.md
provenance.matchedText: Removed the `--concurrent-service-syncs` kube-controller-manager flag (no-op since v1.31). (#138002, @Jefftree) [SIG API Machinery]

rules.title: kubelet eventRecordQPS=0 now means UNLIMITED event-write rate (was silently capped) from Kubernetes 1.37
rules.remediation: A kubelet configuration with eventRecordQPS explicitly set to 0 changes meaning at 1.37: previously (buggy) it was silently treated as the default (50 events/sec); from 1.37 it means truly unlimited Event object creation, which can flood the API server/etcd under load. If you want the old bounded behavior, set eventRecordQPS to 50 explicitly before upgrading to 1.37+.
rules.note: Confirmed eventRecordQPS is a real KubeletConfiguration v1beta1 field (json tag `eventRecordQPS`) and that its coded default is 50 when unset — corroborating that '0' was previously silently coerced to a bounded default rather than truly unlimited before this fix.

provenance.name: kubernetes/kubernetes CHANGELOG-1.37.md
provenance.matchedText: When eventRecordQPS in kubelet configuration file is set to 0, there will be no limit enforced. The bug when 0 value was treated as a default value, while the field description was saying "unlimited" is fixed. if your kubelet configuration setting eventRecordQPS to 0 and you want to preserve the previous behavior, please change the value to 50. Keeping it as 0 will make it undefined. (#117119, @HirazawaUi) [SIG API Machinery, Auth and Node]

provenance.name: k8s.io/kubelet config v1beta1/types.go (field existence + doc comment)
provenance.matchedText: // eventRecordQPS is the maximum event creations per second. If 0, there ... EventRecordQPS *int32 `json:"eventRecordQPS,omitempty"`

provenance.name: kubernetes/kubernetes pkg/kubelet/apis/config/v1beta1/defaults.go (coded default = 50)
provenance.matchedText: if obj.EventRecordQPS == nil { obj.EventRecordQPS = ptr.To[int32](50) }

rules.title: Deprecated cAdvisor flags cause the kubelet to FAIL TO START from Kubernetes 1.37
rules.remediation: Remove any of the deprecated cAdvisor flags (--application-metrics-count-limit, --boot-id-file, --container-hints, --containerd, --containerd-namespace, --enable-load-reader, --event-storage-age-limit, --event-storage-event-limit, --global-housekeeping-interval, --log-cadvisor-usage, --machine-id-file, --storage-driver-user/--storage-driver-password/--storage-driver-host/--storage-driver-db/--storage-driver-table/--storage-driver-secure/--storage-driver-buffer-duration) from your kubelet's command line / systemd unit / extra-args file before upgrading to 1.37+. Only --housekeeping-interval is retained.
rules.note: VERIFIED against the real K8s CHANGELOG-1.37.md (see provenance) — this breaker is 100% real, matching the two starter rules this catalog was scoped to build. NOT DETECTABLE by Phase 3's two collection surfaces: these are legacy CLI-only flags registered directly on the kubelet BINARY's own flag set, never part of the typed KubeletConfiguration struct served by /configz (confirmed by inspecting k8s.io/kubelet/config/v1beta1/types.go, which has ZERO cadvisor/housekeeping-named fields — see the negative-evidence provenance entry below), and the kubelet itself is a host-level process with NO Kubernetes Pod/static-pod representation (unlike kube-apiserver/scheduler/controller-manager), so the retained static-pod command[]/args[] surface cannot see it either. ConfigBreakerAnalyzer explicitly filters out (skips) rules with detectable=false so this entry is NEVER silently reported as 'checked and clean' — it is retained here purely for documentation/backlog (a future host-level collector, e.g. a node DaemonSet reading /proc/1/cmdline or the kubelet systemd unit, would be required to actually detect it).

provenance.name: kubernetes/kubernetes CHANGELOG-1.37.md
provenance.matchedText: DEPRECATION!!! The kubelet's embedded cAdvisor now uses the leaner github.com/google/cadvisor/lib module, which removes three long-deprecated or legacy surfaces: Deprecated cAdvisor flags are no longer accepted and the kubelet will fail to start if any are set (only --housekeeping-interval is kept): --application-metrics-count-limit, --boot-id-file, --container-hints, --containerd, --containerd-namespace, --enable-load-reader, --event-storage-age-limit, --event-storage-event-limit, --global-housekeeping-interval, --log-cadvisor-usage, --machine-id-file, --storage-driver-user, --storage-driver-password, --storage-driver-host, --storage-driver-db, --storage-driver-table, --storage-driver-secure, --storage-driver-buffer-duration. Remove these from your kubelet configuration. (#139870, @dims) [SIG API Machinery, Auth, Instrumentation, Network, Node and Testing]

provenance.name: k8s.io/kubelet config v1beta1/types.go (negative-evidence check)
provenance.matchedText: (grep for 'cadvisor'/'housekeeping' case-insensitive across the full file: zero matches — confirms these flags are NOT part of the typed KubeletConfiguration struct served by /configz)

rules.title: Feature gate `HPAContainerMetrics` was removed in Kubernetes 1.32 — control-plane component fails to start if still set
rules.remediation: Remove `HPAContainerMetrics` from the `--feature-gates` flag on kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, and kube-controller-manager (whichever carry it) before upgrading to 1.32+. A removed/unrecognized feature-gate name causes the component to exit at startup with an 'unrecognized feature-gate' error.
rules.note: Kubernetes feature gates fully removed from the shared apiserver/component-base FeatureGate registry cause a fatal 'unrecognized feature-gate' error at flag-parse time on ANY control-plane binary whose --feature-gates still references the removed name — this is mechanical flag validation, independent of whether that specific binary's code path ever consulted the gate at runtime. Scoped to the three control-plane components (kube-apiserver/kube-scheduler/kube-controller-manager) whose retained static-pod command[]/args[] this catalog's collection surface can see; does NOT cover a bare kubelet process (no static-pod representation) unless a matching kubeletConfig featureGateMap rule also exists for this gate.

provenance.name: kubernetes/kubernetes CHANGELOG-1.35.md (session copy: v135_0.md, identical text confirmed against ch135.md)
provenance.matchedText: Removed the `--pod-infra-container-image` flag from `kubelet` command line. For `non-kubeadm` clusters, users must manually remove this flag from their `kubelet` configuration to prevent startup failures before upgrading `kubelet`. For `kubeadm` clusters, if users pass extra arguments to the `kubelet` like `--pod-infra-container-image`, it will be written to the `kubelet` env file during the `init` phase. `kubeadm` does not remove it during the `init` or `join` phase, so users must manually remove it from `extraArgs` in the `kubelet` configuration file. ([#133779](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133779), [@carlory](https://github.com/carlory))

rules.title: kubelet has explicitly disabled the Kubernetes 1.35 cgroup-v1 startup safety net (failCgroupV1=false)
rules.remediation: This node's kubelet config explicitly sets failCgroupV1=false, overriding the 1.35+ default (true) that makes the kubelet refuse to start on a cgroup v1 host. This is NOT itself proof the host runs cgroup v1 — verify each node's actual cgroup version manually (e.g. `stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup/` — cgroup2fs=v2, tmpfs=v1) before relying on this override, and plan to migrate off cgroup v1 (deprecated) regardless.
rules.note: IMPORTANT DISTINCTION (see step2_summary.md): this rule detects only that the operator has DELIBERATELY disabled the 1.35 safety guard — it does NOT and CANNOT detect whether the node is actually running cgroup v1 (no Kubernetes API/field exposes host cgroup version anywhere; verified against corev1 NodeSystemInfo and KubeletConfiguration v1beta1 — see the node-runtime catalog's own advisory entry for the un-detectable half of this breaker). `failCgroupV1` IS a real, verified KubeletConfiguration v1beta1 field (json tag `failCgroupV1`, default true from 1.35) confirmed present in a real /configz capture during this investigation.

provenance.matchedText:
ACTION REQUIRED: The insecure port flags `--port` may only be set to 0 now.
  
  In addtion, please be careful that:
  - controller-manager MUST start with `--authorization-kubeconfig` and `--authentication-kubeconfig` correctly set to get authentication/authorization working.
  - liveness/readiness probes to controller-manager MUST use HTTPS now, and the default port has been changed to 10257.
  - Applications that fetch metrics from controller-manager should use a dedicated service account which is allowed to access nonResourceURLs `/metrics`. rules.title: Feature gate `DeclarativeValidationTakeover` is LOCKED to its default (false) in Kubernetes 1.37 — setting it to true is rejected
rules.remediation: Kubernetes 1.37 locks `DeclarativeValidationTakeover` to its default of `false` (PreRelease: Deprecated, LockToDefault: true). The gate name is still registered, so passing `DeclarativeValidationTakeover=false` starts normally — but passing `=true` is rejected and the component exits. Remove it from `--feature-gates` on kube-apiserver/kube-scheduler/kube-controller-manager: it is slated for removal in a later release, at which point ANY value becomes a startup failure.
rules.note: CORRECTED 2026-08-28. This rule previously claimed the gate was REMOVED in 1.37 with severity CRITICAL and the text 'control-plane component fails to start if still set'. That is wrong: pkg/features/kube_features.go and staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/features/kube_features.go at tag v1.37.0 both declare {Version: 1.37, Default: false, PreRelease: featuregate.Deprecated, LockToDefault: true} — still registered, still accepted at its default. Any cluster passing DeclarativeValidationTakeover=false received a false CRITICAL/40 saying its apiserver would not boot. Re-banded to MEDIUM (locked) / LOW (deprecated from 1.36). NOTE: the featureGateList condition matches gate PRESENCE, not its value, so this cannot distinguish =true (fatal) from =false (fine) — the remediation text says so explicitly rather than implying certainty the data does not support.
